titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The King of Ethiopia’s First War (ch. 94)
part: ch. 94 — The King of Ethiopia’s First War
about: Menelik, called David, sets out from Məsfəna with the Ark and conquers the lands from Saba to the borders of Egypt, while the Ark carries his army three months’ distance in a day; the chapter closes with a colophon on the book’s finding in Constantinople and the verdict of Dematyos of Antioch.

sentences.i: Chapter 94: The first war of the king of Ethiopia
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ቀዳሚ is “first”; ፀብአ is the noun “war, battle” in the construct state (“war of”), and ንጉሠ is in turn construct before ኢትዮጵያ, so the chain ፀብአ ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ is “war of the king of Ethiopia” (the king is Menelik, here called David, as the text itself does below).

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ተንሥኡ ፡ ለፀብእ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ፫ ፡ አውራኅ ፡ እምነ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፡ ምስለ ፡ ማክዳ ፡ እሙ ፡ ወጽዮን ፡ እግዝእቱ ፡ ወሌዋዊያን ፡ ይጸውርዋ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ሐቢቶሙ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ በብዙኅ ፡ ግርማ ፡ ከመ ፡ አሜሃ ፡ በደብረ ፡ ሲና ፡ አመ ፡ ያወርዳ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምሰማያት ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ በቅድስና ፡ ኀበ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ወአሮን ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ ይጸውርዋ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ሕግ ፡ አዛርያስ ፡ ወኤልሚያስ ፡ ወባዕዳን ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እንዘ ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ በየማና ፡ ወበፀጋማ ፡ በገቦሃ ፡ በፍጽማ ፡ ወበኳላሃ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይሴብሑ ፡ ወይዜምሩ ፡ እንዘ ፡ መሬታዊያን ፡ ከመ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ሰማያዊያን ፤
sentences.l: And-then they-arose for-war after 3 months from city-of ምስፍና with Makeda mother-his and-Zion lady-his, and-Levites they-carry-her the-ark-of law with furnishing-of tent-their(?), and-while they-march in-much awe like then on-mount Sinai when brought-down-her God from-heavens Zion in-holiness to Moses and-Aaron; and-likewise they-carry-her the-ark-of law Azarias and-Elmeyas and-others sons-of host-of Israel, while they-march on-her-right and-on-her-left, at-side-her, at-end-her(?) and-at-behind-her, while they-praise and-sing, while earthly-ones like host-of heavenly-ones;
sentences.i: And then, after three months, they set out for war from the city of Məsfəna, together with Makeda his mother and Zion his lady, and the Levites carried the Ark of the Law with the furnishings of their tent (?). They marched in great awe, as at that time on Mount Sinai when God brought Zion down from heaven in holiness to Moses and Aaron. In the same way Azarias and Elmeyas and the other sons of the host of Israel carried the Ark of the Law, marching on its right and on its left, at its side, at its end (?) and behind it, praising and singing, earthly men like the host of the heavenly ones.
sentences.n: The war-march sets out from Məsfəna (ምስፍና, a place name, also “rule”) with the Ark carried in solemn procession, and the text compares it to the Sinai theophany: the Ark (here called Zion, ጽዮን) is brought down from heaven to Moses and Aaron, so the march is a re-enactment of the giving of the Law. Zion is the Ark itself, spoken of as a person, “his lady.” ይጸውርዋ is “they carry her” (ጾረ, with ‑ዋ “her”; the Ark is feminine). ንዋየ ሐቢቶሙ, “furnishing of their ሐቢት,” is uncertain (?): ሐቢት is not clear to me, perhaps a tent or covering (?). ምስለ and ወ- are “with” and “and”; the construct chains ደቂቀ ኀይለ እስራኤል “sons of the host of Israel” and ታቦተ ሕግ “ark of the law” (ሕግ = law) carry the sense. Azarias is the son of Zadok the high priest, as in the earlier parts; ኤልሚያስ is Elmeyas, one of the companions. በፍጽማ “at its end” (?) and በኳላሃ “behind it” (?) are guesses from context. The unit is 64 words, over the usual cut, but it has no ፤ at which to divide it.

sentences.t: ወወሀቦሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ቃለ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ወዜማ ፡ መንክረ ፡ እስመ ፡ ሠምረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሴባሕ ፡ ቦሙ ፡ ወበጽሑ ፡ እምህገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፡ ተዐየኑ ፡ በማየ ፡ አበው ፡ ወበነግህ ፡ አጥፍእዋ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ዛዉ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሐድያ ፤
sentences.l: And-gave-them God voice good and-melody wonderful, because was-pleased God that he-be-praised through-them; and-they-arrived from-city-of ምስፍና, met(?) at-water-of fathers; and-at-dawn they-destroyed-her the-land-of Zaw with Hadya;
sentences.i: And God gave them a good voice and a wondrous melody, for God was pleased to be praised through them. And they arrived from the city of Məsfəna and came to (?) the water of the fathers (?); and at dawn they destroyed the land of Zaw with Hadya;
sentences.n: The singing is God’s gift, so the march itself praises him. ወወሀቦሙ is ወሀበ “give” with ‑ሙ “them.” In እምህገረ ምስፍና the source prints ህገረ, a slip for ሀገረ “city of”; it is kept as printed. ወበጽሑ እምህገረ is “and they arrived from the city of” (እም- is “from”, not “at”), that is, having come out of Məsfəna. ተዐየኑ is the house word “were seen / met face to face” (?); with a place as object it is read here as “met, came upon, came to” (?), and the same hedge applies wherever it recurs in this part. በማየ አበው “at the water of the fathers” may be a place name (?). አጥፍእዋ is አጠፍአ “destroy” + ‑ዋ “it/her.” ዛዉ and ሐድያ are peoples or lands I take as names (Hadya is the known land of southern Ethiopia); Zaw is unidentified (?).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ጋእዘ ፡ ባ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፡ እምቀዳሚ ፡ ወእምዝ ፡ አጥፍእዎሙ ፡ ወቀተልዎሙ ፡ በአፈ ፡ ኀጺን ፡ ወተኃለፉ ፡ እምህየ ፡ ወተዐየኑ ፡ ጌርሳ ፤
sentences.l: for ጋእዘ(?) in-her(?) with-them from-first; and-then they-destroyed-them and-killed-them by-mouth-of iron, and-passed-on from-there and-met(?) Gersa;
sentences.i: for ጋእዘ (a word I cannot identify (?)) had been among them from of old. Then they destroyed them and killed them by the edge of the sword, and passed on from there and came to (?) Gersa;
sentences.n: ጋእዘ ባ is unclear (?): ጋእዘ might be a name or a verb, and ባ is “in her” (በ with the 3fs suffix -ኣ), but what the “her” refers to is not clear, so the first clause is rendered only as far as it can be read. በአፈ ኀጺን “by the mouth of the sword” is the biblical idiom for the sword’s edge (ኀጺን is literally “iron”). ወተኃለፉ is “and they passed on”; ወተዐየኑ ጌርሳ “and they came to Gersa” (?), a place name I cannot place.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ አጥፍኡ ፡ ህገረ ፡ ሰባድዕት ፡ እለ ፡ ገጾሙ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወዘነበ ፡ አድግ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሐቌሆሙ ፡ ወገብአት ፡ ወተዐየነት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ወነበሩ ፡ ባቲ ፡ እስከ ፡ ፫ ፡ አውራኅ ፡ ወአንሥኡ ፡ ሰረገላቲሆሙ ፡ ወበጽሑ ፡ ህገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፤
sentences.l: And-again they-destroyed land-of Sabadʿət who faces-their men and-tail-of ass at loins-their; and-she-returned and-met(?) into city-of Zion, and-they-stayed in-her until 3 months, and-they-raised carts-their and-arrived city-of ምስፍና;
sentences.i: And again they destroyed the land of the Sabadʿət, whose faces are those of men and who have an ass’s tail at their loins. And she returned and came to (?) the city of Zion, and they stayed in it three months, and they set their carts in motion and reached the city of Məsfəna;
sentences.n: Two source slips, ህገረ for ሀገረ “city, land of,” are kept as printed (here and at the end of the unit). ሰባድዕት is taken as a people’s name (?). The people have men’s faces (ገጾሙ ሰብእ) and an ass’s tail (ዘነበ አድግ, with ዘነበ the construct of ዘነብ “tail”). ወገብአት ወተዐየነት are feminine singular, “she returned and met (?)”; ተዐየነት is the same verb as ተዐየኑ, with the same hedge, and is rendered “came to (?)” in English; the subject is Zion, the Ark (?), the only feminine person in the scene. ባቲ is “in her/it,” the city. ሰረገላ is “cart” (the house word in the earlier parts); ወአንሥኡ ሰረገላቲሆሙ, “they raised their carts,” means they set out (?). እስከ ፫ አውራኅ is “up to three months.”

sentences.t: ወእምህየ ፡ በአሐቲ ፡ ዕለት ፡ በጽሑ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሳባ ፡ ወአጥፍእዋ ፡ ለኖባ ፡ ወእምህየ ፡ ተዐየኑ ፡ ሳባ ፡ ወአጥፍኡ ፡ እስከ ፡ ደወለ ፡ ግብጽ ።
sentences.l: And-from-there in-one day they-arrived land-of Saba and-destroyed-her Noba, and-from-there they-met(?) Saba and-destroyed until boundaries-of Egypt.
sentences.i: And from there in one day they reached the land of Saba and destroyed Noba; and from there they came to (?) Saba and destroyed as far as the borders of Egypt.
sentences.n: A journey in a single day shows the miraculous speed the text goes on to describe. ሳባ is Saba (Sheba), ኖባ Noba (Nubia, ?). ደወለ ግብጽ “boundaries of Egypt” keeps the house reading of ደወል “border” as a construct. በአሐቲ ዕለት is “in one day.”

sentences.t: ወኮነ ፡ ግርማ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ ለንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እስከ ፡ ያመጽኡ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ምድያም ፡ ወንጉሠ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ወበጽሑ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፡ ወእምህየ ፡ ተዐየኑ ፡ አብዓት ፡ ወፀብኡ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ህንደኬ ፤
sentences.l: And-became awe great for-king-of Ethiopia until they-brought gift king-of Midian and-king-of Egypt, and-arrived into city-of ምስፍና; and-from-there met(?) Abʿat(?) and-fought into sea-of Candace;
sentences.i: And the king of Ethiopia was held in great awe, until the king of Midian and the king of Egypt brought gifts, and they reached the city of Məsfəna. From there they met (?) Abʿat (?) and fought at the sea of Candace;
sentences.n: ወኮነ ግርማ ዐቢይ ለንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ is literally “there was great awe for the king of Ethiopia,” that is, the awe he inspired in others; ለ‑ marks whose it is. The “enemies” are not in the Geʿez. The “they” who reach Məsfəna and then go on to meet (?) Abʿat and fight are, I take it, the Ethiopians (?). እስከ ያመጽኡ is “until they brought,” with አምኃ “gifts, tribute.” Midian and Egypt now pay tribute. አብዓት is unclear (?), perhaps a place name. ባሕረ ህንደኬ “sea of Candace” takes ህንደኬ as the Ethiopian queen’s title (Acts 8); here it is a land or its king, as the next unit shows.

sentences.t: ወአብአ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ህንደኬ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ወጋዳ ፡ ወሰገደ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ለንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወኀበ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘፈቀደ ፡ ወፀብአ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይመውኦ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ዘይመውእ ፡ ለሊሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-brought king-of Candace gift and-gada(?), and-bowed himself to-king-of Ethiopia; and-to every which he-wished and-fought none who-overcomes-him except who overcomes, himself;
sentences.i: And the king of Candace brought gifts and gada (?), and he himself bowed down before the king of Ethiopia. Wherever he wished and fought, none could overcome him, except he who overcomes, himself (?);
sentences.n: ወጋዳ keeps the house reading of ጋዳ as some kind of gift (?). ሰገደ is “bowed down, did homage.” ለሊሁ is the emphatic “himself.” ዘይመውኦ is “who would overcome him” (ሞዐ “conquer, overcome”, as in ch. 88), and ዘእንበለ ዘይመውእ ለሊሁ, “except he who conquers, himself,” is obscure (?): taken literally, no one overcomes him but the one who overcomes, himself; it may mean that the king is his own conqueror, so that no other can be.

sentences.t: ወእለ ፡ ያስተሓይጽዎ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ትዕይንቱ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይስምዑ ፡ ዜና ፡ ወይንግሩ ፡ ለሀገሮሙ ፡ ወኢይክሉ ፡ ረዊጸ ፡ በሰረገላ ፡ እስመ ፡ ለሊሃ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ታደክም ፡ ኀይሎሙ ፡ ለፀር ።
sentences.l: And-those-who they-watch-him-closely(?) in-midst host-his that they-hear news and-tell for-lands-their and-not-they-can to-run in-cart, because himself Zion she-wearies strength-their for-enemy.
sentences.i: And those who watch him closely (?) in the midst of his host, so that they may hear the news and tell it to their own lands, are not able to run in a cart, for Zion herself wearies the strength of the enemy.
sentences.n: The sense of ያስተሓይጽዎ is uncertain (?): I read it, with the house entry (ch. 25, 30), as “those who watch him closely,” the enemy’s spies or observers who would carry the news home. ትዕይንቱ I take as “his host in array” (the house reading of ትዕይንት, ?). ከመ ይስምዑ ወይንግሩ is “that they may hear and tell.” ረዊጸ is “to run” (the infinitive of the verb in ይረውጹ below), said of travelling by cart; “to flee” would be a guess. ታደክም is the causative “she makes weary”; ለሊሃ ጽዮን, “Zion herself,” makes the Ark the fighter, not the army.

sentences.t: ወንጉሥሰ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሰራዊቱ ፡ ወሰራዊተ ፡ ሰራዊቱ ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ይትኤዘዙ ፡ በቃሉ ፡ ይረው ፡ ጹ ፡ በሰረገላ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ደዌ ፡ ወሕማም ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ወጽምእ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሃፍ ፡ ወድካም ፡ ይበጽሑ ፡ በአሐቲ ፡ ዕለት ፡ መጠነ ፡ ምሕዋረ ፡ ፫ ፡ አውራኅ ፤
sentences.l: And-king-indeed David with army-his and-army-of army-his and-all who obey by-word-his ይረው ፡ ጹ in-cart without illness and-pain, without hunger and-thirst, without ሃፍ(?) and-weariness, they-arrive in-one day measure-of journey-of 3 months;
sentences.i: As for King David, with his army and the army of his army, and all who obey his word, they run in carts without illness and pain, without hunger and thirst, without faintness (?) and weariness, and they arrive in one day, as far as a journey of three months;
sentences.n: ንጉሥ ዳዊት is Menelik, who took his father’s name David when crowned. ‑ሰ in ወንጉሥሰ means “as for.” The source prints ይረው ፡ ጹ, a split of ይረውጹ “they run” (ሮጸ, as in ረዊጸ above); kept as printed. ሰራዊተ ሰራዊቱ is “the army of his army,” the second rank. ይትኤዘዙ is “they obey.” ሃፍ is unclear (?), I take it as “faintness.” The pairs ዘእንበለ ደዌ ወሕማም “without illness and pain” show the Ark’s protection of the marchers. መጠነ ምሕዋረ ፫ አውራኅ is “as much as the journey of three months.”

sentences.t: ወአልቦ ፡ ወኢምንተኒ ፡ ዘየኀጥኡ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ሰአሉ ፡ በኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በውስተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ እስመ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ይነብር ፡ ምስሌሃ ፡ ወመልአኩ ፡ ይሜግባ ፡ ወማኅደሩ ፡ ለሊሃ ፤
sentences.l: And-not-there-is and-nothing which they-lack of-what they-asked of God in-Zion, ark-of law-his of-God, because himself he-dwells with-her and-angel-his he-moves-her(?) and-dwelling-his herself;
sentences.i: And there is nothing at all that they lack of what they asked of God in Zion, the Ark of God’s law, for he himself dwells with her, and his angel moves her (?), and she is his dwelling place;
sentences.n: ወአልቦ ወኢምንተኒ is “and there is not anything at all.” ዘየኀጥኡ is “which they miss / lack.” እምዘ ሰአሉ በኀበ እግዚኣብሔር is “of that which they asked from God.” ይሜግባ keeps the house reading “he moves her (?),” here as the angel who bears or leads the Ark. ማኅደር is “dwelling,” so the Ark is God’s house; the passage’s core idea is that God himself dwells with Zion.

sentences.t: ወለንጉሥ ፡ ዘይትለአክ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ደብተራሁ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ሖረ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ፍኖቱ ፡ ወበገቢረ ፡ ፈቃዲ ፡ ይትገበር ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘፈቀደ ፡ ወዘኀለየ ፡ በልቡ ፡ ወዘአንጸረ ፡ በአጽባዕቱ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ይትገበር ፡ በቃሉ ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ይፈርሆ ፤
sentences.l: And-for-king who he-serves at tent-his, if he-goes in-all way-his, and-in-doing will-his it-is-done all which he-wishes and-which he-thinks in-heart-his and-which he-points(?) with-fingers-his, all it-is-done by-word-his and-all they-fear-him;
sentences.i: And for the king who serves (?) at his tent, if he goes on any of his ways, then in the doing of his will everything is done that he wishes, and whatever he thinks in his heart, and whatever he points to (?) with his fingers; all is done at his word, and all fear him;
sentences.n: ዘይትለአክ is the tä-stem of ለአከ “serve, minister” (3ms imperfect; “is sent” is also possible, as in ch. 25) (?): ደብተራ is the tent (tabernacle), and the king is the one who ministers at it, as David did before Zion. ፈቃዲ is “his will” (-ዲ for -ሁ, Bezold’s spelling, as in the earlier parts). ይትገበር is the passive “it is done.” ዘፈቀደ ወዘኀለየ ወዘአንጸረ is the three “whatever he wished, thought, pointed at,” where አንጸረ (“looked toward, regarded” in ch. 49–50) is rendered “points to (?)” only as a guess from በአጽባዕቱ “with his fingers.” ወኵሉ ይፈርሆ “and all fear him.”

sentences.t: ወውእቱሰ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይፈርህ ፡ እስመ ፡ እደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ እንተ ፡ ተዐቅቦ ፡ ሌሊተ ፡ ወመዐልተ ፡ እስመ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ፈቃዶ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወየዐቅቦ ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ እኩይ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፨
sentences.l: And-he-indeed none who he-fears, because hand-of God with-him which she-guards-him night and-day, because he-did will-his; and-he-also he-does for-him and-he-guards-him from-all evil for-world-of world Amen
sentences.i: But as for him, there is no one he fears, for the hand of God is with him, which guards him night and day, because he did his will (?). And he in his turn does it for him, and he guards him from all evil, for ever and ever. Amen.
sentences.n: ወውእቱሰ “but as for him” turns from the people’s fear of the king to the king’s freedom from fear. እደ እግዚኣብሔር, “the hand of God,” is feminine here, hence እንተ ተዐቅቦ “which guards him.” ገብረ ፈቃዶ “he did his will”: whose will is not marked. Since ወውእቱኒ ይገብር ሎቱ means “and he in turn does for him,” I take it that God did the king’s will and the king now does God’s (?); the other reading, the king doing God’s will, is possible. The closing ለዓለመ ዓለም አሜን, “for ever and ever, Amen,” ends the chapter; one ፨ follows.

sentences.t: ዘንተ ፡ ረከብኩ ፡ እመጻሕፍት ፡ ዘቤተ ፡ ሶፍያ ፡ ዘቊስጥንጥንያ ፨
sentences.l: This I-found from-books of-house-of Sophia of-Constantinople
sentences.i: This I found in the books of the church of Sophia in Constantinople.
sentences.n: Colophon: here the narrator, or the compiler, speaks in the first person and names the Church of Hagia Sophia (ሶፍያ) in Constantinople (ቊስጥንጥንያ) as the place where the book was found. ዘቤተ ሶፍያ is “of the house of Sophia,” and the following ዘቊስጥንጥንያ “of Constantinople.” ረከብኩ is the first-person perfect “I found.” The point is to give the book an authority from the great church of the East.

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎ ፡ እለ ፡ ህየ ፡ ሊቃነ ፡ ጳጳሳት ፡ አማንኬ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ዘተጽሕፈ ፡ እመዋዕለ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ።
sentences.l: And-they-said-to-him those there chiefs-of bishops: Is-it-true this which was-written from-days-of Solomon king.
sentences.i: And the archbishops there said to him, “Is it true, this which was written from the days of King Solomon?”
sentences.n: The clergy of Constantinople ask whether the book goes back to Solomon’s time. ወይቤልዎ is “and they said to him”; ሊቃነ ጳጳሳት “chiefs of the bishops” is a construct, perhaps patriarchs or archbishops. ‑ኬ in አማንኬ marks a question. Who “him” is, the finder or the translator, is not stated.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ድማትዮስ ፡ ዘአንጾኪያ ፡ እወ ፡ ይመስል ፡ እስከ ፡ ዕለተ ፡ ሞቱ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ዘተጽሕፈ ፡ ወእምድኅረ ፡ ሞቱሰ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ እምባዕዳን ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ዘተጽሕፈ ፡ አምሳሉ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-said Dəmatyos of-Antioch: Yes, it-seems until day-of death-his for-Solomon which was-written, and-after death-his-indeed for-Solomon from-other prophets which was-written likeness-his. ፨ ፨ ፨ …
sentences.i: And Dematyos of Antioch said, “Yes, what was written seems true up to the day of Solomon’s death. But after his death, as for what was written, it is like it, from other prophets (?).” (The text ends with a row of nine ፨ signs.)
sentences.n: Colophon, continued (ይመስል is “it resembles, it seems”): Dematyos of Antioch (ድማትዮስ, the same name as the Dematyos of Rome in ch. 18; he is not identified with Demetrius) answers that the text is accepted up to Solomon’s death, and after that it is written in the manner of other prophets (?). The last clause, እምባዕዳን ነቢያት ዘተጽሕፈ አምሳሉ, is uncertain (?): “from other prophets, what was written, its likeness.” The row of ፨ signs closes the whole book, attached to this last unit as in earlier parts.
